program: Housing research, policy analysis and implementation advocacy

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-final-four-independent-acceptance.json: original-return checks and independent numerical reconstruction; accepted only as explicit conditional alpha hypotheses, not measured causal estimates.

what: CHPC researches housing policy and advocates practical implementation changes in New York City.
Its basement work seeks safe legalization, but CHPC does not directly build or provide housing.
A conditional basement-health pathway estimates $129.9 million per 10 local QALYs using two years of the entire recipient's cost.
strengths: A specific implementation agenda can potentially influence many homes.
Original returns permit recovery of event expenses omitted from headline costs.
The report accounts for existing legislation and city investment before assigning incremental advocacy credit.
reservations: Potential apartments and policy recommendations are not completed safety upgrades.
A donation's effect on implementation, occupancy and health remains unmeasured.
Construction costs, tenant displacement and exclusion of flood-prone homes can materially change net benefit.

sections.what: Citizens Housing and Planning Council of New York Inc., EIN 13-1782468, researches housing, land use and neighborhood policy. It is distinct from the Massachusetts Citizens' Housing and Planning Association and from NYC housing agencies. The January 2026 agenda includes basement implementation, affordable-housing pipelines, costs and land-use administration; an ordinary gift supports this entire agenda. [Current recommendations](https://chpcny.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Housing-Recommendations-for-a-New-Administration-1.pdf)
sections.monitoring: Track CHPC recommendations adopted beyond existing plans, the implementation change attributable to its work, actual safe occupied units and the timing difference versus baseline. Record displaced tenants, return rates, rents, remediated moisture, functioning egress/fire protection and injuries. CHPC's2016 Hidden Housing study estimated10,000–38,000 potential apartments under then-existing zoning; it is a technical opportunity estimate, not a current approved pipeline or measured output. [Original research summary](https://chpcny.org/publication/hidden-housing/)
sections.qualitative: The scalable mechanism is making already-occupied unsafe homes safer sooner. Existing residents already have some shelter, so legal status and property appreciation receive no automatic QALYs. Current DOB rules describe a 10-year legalization route and exclude high-risk flood locations; it would be wrong to assign protection from every future Ida-like death to eligible conversions. [Current program](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/codes/adu.page) The2025 proposed rules specify egress, alarms and later sprinklers/flood sensors, plus tenant return procedures. [Safety mechanism](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/dob/pr-legalizing-basement.page) A small randomized housing-moisture remediation trial supports a respiratory-health mechanism for symptomatic asthmatic children receiving combined home and clinical intervention; the model's population prevalence and QALY conversion are separate judgments. [Trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1626393/)
sections.cost: Two years of full gross recipient cost total $3,705,810. The conditional model considers1,000 safely implemented units influenced by a possible administrative improvement, then applies 0.25 incremental implementation probability, 0.2 CHPC share and 0.5 financing response: 25 attributable unit-equivalents, or 0.00675 per $1,000. These are expected-value modeling units, not homes sold by CHPC. With 80% occupancy and 2 residents each, 40 attributable resident-equivalents receive at most five years of safer conditions beginning year2. Annual injury risk 0.0002, 50% risk reduction, 10% fatal severity and 0.3 nonfatal QALYs are judgments. Fatal gains have20-year survival cap, 0.8 utility, 2% mortality and 3% discount. Separately10% of residents receive 0.02 annual utility through respiratory improvement; no lifetime cure is assumed. A 20% offset allows displacement/other housing harms. Central benefit is 0.285329 local QALYs. The1-year acceleration scenario is relevant if baseline implementation catches up quickly.
sections.funding: FY2024 Form 990 expense is $1,571,694, but Part VIII also nets $281,211 event costs from revenue; full gross recipient cost is $1,852,905. FY2023 analogously adds $259,755 to $1,617,518 for $1,877,273. Schedule D repeats the net presentation; it does not eliminate the real event resources. FY2024 net assets total $2,501,602, of which $2,364,762 are unrestricted. [2024 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202503219349311945/IRS990) [2023 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202443209349311019/IRS990) No costed unfunded implementation position was located; reserves and broad advocacy scope make 0.5 gift responsiveness uncertain. The mayor reported more than $1 million invested in the city legalization effort by August 2026; this continues in the counterfactual and is not assigned to CHPC. [Current public baseline](https://www.nyc.gov/bn/mayors-office/news/2026/08/transcript--mayor-mamdani-holds-ethnic-and-community-media-round) Recipient expense excludes owners' retrofit and public administration costs; an illustrative25 attributed units*$50,000=$1.25 million addition shows one resource sensitivity, not measured construction cost.

model.costScope: Two full annual gross recipient cost-equivalents including event expenses; other housing-policy effects provisionally netzero; induced construction cost separate.
model.geographicAttribution: All modeled safe occupancy is within NYC, therefore inside22-county OMB23-01 MSA; no benefit extrapolated to restofMSA or other states.
model.formula: A=sum(t=start..start+T-1)exp(-m*(t-start+1))/(1+d)^t; D=sum(t=1..L)u*exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; U=N*p*a*b; Qall=U*o*n*A*(R*e*(f*D+(1-f)*j)+s*v)*(1-x)-h; Qlocal=g*Qall; cost=C*Y+publicCost; price10=10*cost/Qlocal if positive.
model.counterfactual: Existing state/local legislation, DOB/HPD staffing, funded city pilot, homeowners and other advocates proceed. Only additional or accelerated safety outcomes get credit; modeled five-year catch-up gap is uncertain.
model.attribution: N conditional units relevant to this mixed advocacy portfolio; p incremental implementation chance, a CHPC causal share, b net financing response. No whole-city housing stock or coalition-wide outcome is credited. Public funding is baseline, not private gift leverage automatically.
model.uncertainty: Very weak conditional partial-health model; potential technical capacity, causal implementation, incremental timing and health all uncertain. Scenarios are hypotheses, not confidence intervals. N=1000 is an illustrative implementation scale with no verified current pipeline. No actual unit production or adoption attributable to CHPC is established.
model.nativeOutcomes: Policy implementation change -> completed, occupied, safer homes -> finite respiratory and injury health.
model.nativeCosts: Central25 attributable safe unit-equivalents over two-year recipient cost, $148,232 per equivalent. Actual direct service output is policy analysis, not units provided.

sensitivity: If city implementation happens anyway or CHPC has no influence, price is undefined because health benefit is zero.
Five-year advantage can be too long where public baseline accelerates; one-year catch-up sensitivity makes this explicit.
Mortality and respiratory effects are separately serialized; injury-only removes the larger morbidity hypothesis. Displacement can exceed modeled gains.
